mainProgression.progression: Em - G - Am - Em - Bm7 - Am7 - C - G - F - C - D
mainProgression.description: Timeless 10-bar ballad progression featuring thumb-over bass movement, double-stop suspensions, and an ethereal borrowed F chord

sectionProgressions.progression: Em - G - Am - Em - Bm7 - Am7 - C - G - F - C - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: vi - I - ii - vi - iii7 - ii7 - IV - I - bVII - IV - V
sectionProgressions.description: The borrowed F major chord (bVII) creates an unexpected, floating modal shift before resolving smoothly through C and D

sectionProgressions.progression: Em - G - Am - Em - Bm7 - Am7 - C - G - F - C - D
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: vi - I - ii - vi - iii7 - ii7 - IV - I - bVII - IV - V
sectionProgressions.description: Played with Leslie rotary speaker modulation, mixing octave glides, singing sustained bends, and microtonal vibrato

harmonicFunction: Em (vi) - The melancholic home base chord fretted with thumb-over-neck bass
G (I) - Uplifts the mood with major pentatonic sliding third decorations
Am (ii) - Smooth stepwise motion decorated with classic 4th-interval suspensions
Bm7 (iii7) - Bittersweet minor tension descending back into Am7
F (bVII) - The harmonic secret: borrowed Mixolydian chord providing a weightless lift
D (V) - Dominant turnaround providing strong gravitational pull back to Em

techniques.name: Thumb-Over Fretting & Bass Movement
techniques.description: Wrapping the fretting-hand thumb over the top of the neck to fret bass notes on the 6th string, freeing the fingers for chord embellishments

notes: Fret the low root note with the fretting-hand thumb
Keep the other four fingers free to add ornamental hammer-ons
Maintain consistent palm muting for selective bass separation
Requires a comfortable guitar neck profile
sequence: Strike bass note with thumb downstroke
Pluck or sweep upper chord tones
Execute hammer-on or slide with pinky/ring finger
Let bass ring while releasing ornamentation
tips: Drop the wrist slightly to wrap the thumb without straining the forearm
Ensure the 5th string is naturally muted with the fleshy thumb pad when not fretted
Practice moving between Em, G, and Am shapes slowly

techniques.name: Double-Stop Hammer-Ons & Slides
techniques.description: Sounding two strings simultaneously and hammering on or sliding on one or both strings, the cornerstone of the Hendrix R&B rhythm style

notes: Commonly executed across the G and B strings or D and G strings
Combines 4th and 5th intervals that resolve into diatonic 3rds
Creates the impression of rhythm guitar and lead guitar playing together
sequence: Barre index finger across two strings
Hammer ring finger one whole step up on the lower string
Slide both fingers upward while maintaining string pressure
tips: Focus on pick control so you only strike the two intended strings
Keep fret fingers curved to avoid choking adjacent strings

techniques.name: Leslie Rotary Modulation & Dynamic Touch
techniques.description: Managing pick velocity to shift between delicate chime and warm saturation through a rotary speaker simulator

notes: Hendrix routed his Stratocaster through a rotating Leslie cabinet in the studio
Pick lightly near the neck pickup for warm acoustic-like shimmer
Dig in on bends for singing compressed sustain
sequence: Roll volume back to 7 for verses, 10 for solo
Add slight Uni-Vibe or chorus modulation
tips: Vary your picking point between bridge and neck

sections.name: Intro Chord-Melody
sections.description: The legendary instrumental statement of the 10-bar progression featuring intricate hammer-ons, slides, and double-stops over ringing bass notes
sections.progression: Em - G - Am - Em - Bm7 - Am7 - C - G - F - C - D
notes: Start with the gentle open E minor arpeggio and pinky hammer-on on the G string
Thumb frets the 3rd fret on low E for G major, allowing index and ring to embellish frets 3 and 5
Notice the dynamic lift on the borrowed F major chord before resolving to D

sections.name: Verse 1
sections.description: Jimi supports his vocals with restrained chord grips and sweet fill-ins during vocal pauses
sections.progression: Em - G - Am - Em - Bm7 - Am7 - C - G - F - C - D
notes: Back off volume slightly to leave acoustic space for the vocal narrative
Fill the vocal gaps with short double-stop licks on the G and B strings
Emphasize the bass notes on beat 1 of each measure

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: One of the most expressive solos in rock history: singing sustained bends, subtle vibrato, and Leslie swirl fading into the distance
sections.progression: Em - G - Am - Em - Bm7 - Am7 - C - G - F - C - D
notes: Begin with high-register melodic bends targeting the B and G notes on the top strings
Use wide vocal-like vibrato with the wrist
Fade out with glissando slides and ambient wah/rotary sweeps

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster with maple or rosewood neck (single-coil pickups)
alternatives: Any SSS or HSS electric guitar with low-output pickups
guitar.pickup: Neck pickup or Neck + Middle pickup in position 4 for signature quack and warmth

amp.recommended: Marshall JTM45 or 1959 Super Lead / Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face (Germanium or Silicon) set with guitar volume rolled back
effects.reverb: Subtle plate or studio spring reverb
effects.other: Leslie rotating speaker simulator / Uni-Vibe, VOX Wah pedal

beginner.title: Learn Chord Framework & Song Flow
steps: Master the 10-bar chord progression using basic open chords (Em, G, Am, Bm, C, F, D)
Practice the timing with a metronome at 60 BPM
Understand the Roman numeral analysis and the borrowed F major chord

intermediate.title: Thumb-Over Technique & Core Embellishments
steps: Integrate the thumb-over fretting technique on G, Am, and F chords
Learn the signature double-stop hammer-ons on the G and B strings
Practice synchronizing bass notes on beat 1 with upper-string chord decorations

advanced.title: Full Studio Intro & Expressive Solo Phrasing
steps: Master the intro note-for-note with exact microtonal bends and dynamics
Integrate rotary speaker/vibe modulation and volume-knob tone shaping
Improvise authentic Hendrix-style embellishments over the 10-bar progression

commonMistakes: Tensing the fretting hand while attempting thumb-over chords—drop the wrist down
Strumming all strings indiscriminately rather than isolating bass notes and double-stops
Rushing the tempo—the ballad feel requires deep pocket and dynamic restraint at 71 BPM
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Warm up with E minor and G major pentatonic double-stop exercises
10 min: Practice thumb-over grips and clean bass-to-treble string separation
15 min: Work on the 10-bar intro measure by measure at 55 BPM
10 min: Play along with the original recording focusing on touch dynamics
focusAreas: Double-stop hammer-on intonation and clean ringing notes
Subtle dynamic control between light strums and accented notes
metronomeWork: Start the intro chord-melody at 50 BPM with quarter-note clicks
Progressively build to 71 BPM once hammer-on timing is completely seamless
